Data & methodology

What the colors mean

A salary is compared with the four OFLC thresholds for the selected occupation, all industries. The catalog includes 848 SOC occupations and 997 O*NET entries. Software Developers (SOC 15-1252) is the default. O*NET entries use the explicit SOC mapping in the OFLC crosswalk. There is no Level V.

  • Deep red: below Level I.
  • Red: at least Level I, below Level II.
  • Yellow: at least Level II, below Level III.
  • Light green: at least Level III, below Level IV.
  • Green: at least Level IV.
  • Gray: missing, flagged, ambiguous or invalid comparison data.

Annual equivalents use 2,080 hours (40 hours × 52 weeks). Threshold comparisons use cents, not rounded whole-dollar labels. The pay input is base salary, excluding equity and bonuses. Counties are counted equally, not weighted by population or available jobs.

Rows labeled Annual Wage already contain annual rates; they are not multiplied by 2,080. Their hourly display is an equivalent. High Wage and No Leveled Wage rows do not publish four levels and remain gray with an explanation. Average wages are never used to invent missing levels.

The catalog and rates are built from ALC_Export.csv, oes_soc_occs.csv and xwalk_plus.csv. Higher-education data (EDC_Export.csv) is not mixed with all-industries data. Only the selected SOC's rates are fetched; salary comparisons remain in the browser. A failed download clears the comparison instead of retaining another occupation's wages.

Wages & geography

Wage data is the October 2026 local snapshot of the DOL OFLC 2026–27 release, effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. This website does not automatically download or apply future releases. A warning appears outside the effective period.

Boundaries are the 2025 U.S. Census 1:5,000,000 cartographic boundaries. The map covers all 50 states & DC, including county equivalents such as independent cities and Connecticut planning regions. Alaska & Hawaii are inset. Territories are not included. Boundary simplification is for visualization, not parcel-level worksite decisions.

Counties are joined by normalized full legal name plus state, with no fuzzy matching. Each county receives its OFLC wage area's rates, not an independently estimated county rate. Adjacent counties may share rates. The generated data records unmatched/ambiguous joins and source metadata.

Limitations

This is a wage comparison, not an official prevailing wage determination, a legal assessment, or a prediction of visa eligibility. An actual role's required wage level is not determined by salary alone. A green county is not a guarantee that a job or application qualifies.

Open source & privacy

Application code is MIT licensed. Map rendering uses D3 (ISC) & icons use Lucide (ISC). Attribution and license texts ship with the source. Salary calculations, search & CSV exports run in your browser. The application sends no salary or location queries to third-party APIs. URLs can contain the chosen salary, county and occupation for bookmarking; standard hosting logs and access controls are outside the application's control.

To update the data, rebuild the extension's wage JSON, run scripts/build-map.py with the new JSON and Census files, and run scripts/build-occupations.py with the same release's unmodified CSV directory. Run the tests, then publish the regenerated dist/ folder. See the source README for exact commands. Never copy your resume folder or personal documents into a deployment.
